questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.topic: Angle revealed by a dot product
questions.stem: Memo 1 from the city planning desk notes vectors u=(3,4) and v=(4,3) and asks which statement about angles is correct.

options.text: The dot product and magnitudes determine cosine of the angle.
The dot product alone equals the angle in degrees.
options.misconception: equates dot product directly with angle measure

options.text: The cross product gives the angle through dot product.
options.misconception: confuses cross product with angle via dot product

options.text: The magnitude of one vector determines the angle.
options.misconception: thinks one magnitude determines angle

questions.explanation: Cosine of the angle equals dot product divided by the product of magnitudes. The dot product alone is not an angle.

questions.stem: Memo 50 from the city planning desk evaluates (12,5) dot (5,12); a student's work is flawed; which option states correct principle?

options.text: Add corresponding components and multiply.
options.misconception: adds components before multiplying

options.text: Multiply corresponding components and add.
Multiply all four components together.
options.misconception: multiplies all components without pairing

options.text: Subtract corresponding components.
options.misconception: subtracts components instead of multiplying

questions.explanation: The dot product is 12*5+5*12=120. Adding components first would be wrong.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.stem: Memo 52 from the city planning desk asks why opposite vectors have cos=-1.

answer.exemplar: For opposite vectors, dot product is negative product of magnitudes, so cosine is -1 and angle is 180 degrees.

questions.explanation: When vectors point opposite ways, the ratio dot/(|u||v|) is -1. Arccos of -1 is 180.

questions.stem: Memo 55 from the city planning desk solves for y with (3,7) perpendicular to (2,y); which principle is correct?

options.text: Set components equal and solve.
options.misconception: equates components instead of dot product

options.text: Set cross product equal to zero and solve.
options.misconception: uses cross product instead of dot product

options.text: Set magnitudes equal and solve.
options.misconception: equates magnitudes instead of dot product

options.text: Set dot product equal to zero and solve.

questions.explanation: Perpendicularity gives 3*2+7*y=0, so y=-6/7. Magnitude equality is not required.
